styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Le Panier lanes, MuCEM and the old port.

styles.label: Beaches
styles.blurb: Calanques coves and Prado city sand.

stays.why: The harbour is the city's front door: ferries, metro and most sights within walking distance.
Old-town lanes above the port, close to MuCEM and the cathedral; quiet at night, steep streets.
Central and cheaper, on the main boulevard between the port and the stations; busier and noisier.
Beachside strip south of the centre; good for swimming and long walks, further from the old town.

food: Try bouillabaisse once, but it is a proper sit-down meal: expect roughly €35–70 per person, and book ahead.
Cheaper and just as local: panisse (chickpea fries), navettes biscuits and a pastis at a port café.
Go to the fish market on the Quai des Belges at the Vieux-Port in the morning; it closes early.
Noailles market area is the place for cheap North African and Middle Eastern food, roughly €8–15 a meal.
Aperitif hour is a local ritual: many bars do cheaper drinks and small plates in the early evening.
more_time: Take the boat to the Frioul islands (about €10 return) for a half-day of rocky coves and sea views.
Swap a city afternoon for Cassis by train: short ride, then a boat to the calanques if the sea is calm.
If you have a car-free day, ride bus and cable car up to Notre-Dame de la Garde for the best view; check opening hours on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the old port, Le Panier and MuCEM, with time for a beach or calanques afternoon; add a night for a Cassis or Frioul day.

month_notes: January: cold and windy, highs near 11°C. Pack a warm layer and expect a few wet days.
February: still cool at 13°C highs; quiet streets and short queues at museums.
March: mild at 15°C, good for walking; rain on about six days.
April: warming to 17°C; pleasant for the old town, sea still cool for swimming.
May: 21°C and mostly dry; a great month for the calanques and long walks.
June: 25°C and only about five rain days; beach season starts properly.
July: hot and very dry at 28°C; go sightseeing early and expect crowds.
August: as hot as July and busy with holidaymakers; book restaurants ahead.
September: 24°C and warm sea; one of the best months for beach plus city.
October: 20°C with more rain (about eight days); carry a light rain jacket.
November: cooler at 16°C and the wettest month, around nine rain days.
December: 13°C highs and chilly evenings; festive port atmosphere, pack layers.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean climate: mild winters, hot dry summers and a windy, sometimes wet spring and autumn.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Highs of 21–28°C and little rain. Ideal for the port, beaches and calanques.

items.title: July and August are hot
items.text: Around 28°C by day and 20–21°C at night. Sightsee in the morning; rest in the afternoon.

items.title: Wettest in autumn
items.text: October and November bring the most rain days (about eight to nine). Showers can be heavy but short.

items.title: The mistral wind
items.text: A strong, cold north wind can blow any season. It clears the sky but makes the sea rough and boat trips uncertain.

items.title: Sea swimming
items.text: Comfortable roughly June to September. Outside that, beaches are for walking, not swimming.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes and sunscreen for summer, a windproof layer and rain jacket for spring and autumn, warm layers for winter.

transit.best: Metro and tram for the centre; walk Le Panier and the port.

modes.text: Two lines, running 05:00–00:30. Single ticket €1.70, or €15 for ten.
Three lines until 00:30, same tickets as the metro. Handy along the main boulevards.
Good coverage, but most routes stop after 21:00. Night buses are limited, so plan evening trips around that.
Taxis exist but watch for rogue drivers. Uber and similar apps work and are often easier.
Not recommended in the centre: narrow streets and parking problems. Useful only for day trips out of town.
Best way to see the Vieux-Port and Le Panier, though the old town is steep in places.
Le vélo scheme costs €1 a week with the first 30 minutes free. Few cycle paths, so ride carefully.
Boat across the Vieux-Port and to Frioul island, about €10 return. Check sailings on the day if windy.
